summary: Lower live indirect grids to workgroup-uniform device-side virtual loops for CUDA/Ascend; share live state copies, six cache swaps and color conditions with Metal.
regressions: Real Metal tests passed for zero work, multiple virtual waves, partial groups, capacity clamping and shared-memory reuse, plus a fresh Rust-reference 129-body LBVH case. CUDA/Ascend shared-memory and argument source checks passed.

Frame manifest regression verifies the added dispatch argument against the original grid, preserving gate mappings and rejecting altered capacity/arguments. Full-scene preparation exposed compiler-generated float pointer views; Ascend wrapper now preserves those views and checks exact argument order.
differences: At most 256 physical groups emulate virtual dispatch without CPU count readback. Cooperative launches retain their original shape. Ascend uses its own SIMT thread binding. Dynamic shared-memory sizes come from compiler metadata. No arithmetic or tolerance change; actual CUDA/Ascend compiler/device synchronization and performance remain unqualified.
